identity.title: CauKer: Classification Time Series Foundation Models Can Be Pretrained on Synthetic Data

problem.claim: TSFMs typically require costly pretraining on large, carefully curated real-world sequence collections.

contributions.claim: CauKer generates diverse, causally coherent synthetic time series with realistic trends, seasonality, and nonlinear interactions.
It combines GP kernel composition with SCMs to support sample-efficient pretraining across classification TSFMs with different architectures and pretraining approaches.
The authors report clear scaling laws for synthetic datasets across dataset size and model capacity, unlike the irregular scaling behavior of real-world datasets.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe CauKer as a novel algorithm for generating synthetic time series for sample-efficient TSFM pretraining.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report clear scaling laws as dataset size increases from 10K to 10M samples.
The authors report clear scaling laws as model capacity increases from 1M to 783M parameters, contrasting with irregular scaling on real-world datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: TSFMs attract interest because of reported zero-shot capabilities and real-world applications.
Their usual pretraining depends on computationally costly, curated real-world sequences.
CauKer combines GP kernel composition and SCMs to generate realistic, causally coherent synthetic data for sample-efficient classification-TSFM pretraining.
Experiments report regular scaling behavior over dataset sizes of 10K–10M and model capacities of 1M–783M, unlike real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links the proposed data generator to explicit variation in dataset size and model capacity, then reports scaling behavior over stated ranges.

lessons.interpretation: A method claim becomes more informative when paired with a measurable resource-scaling axis and a comparison condition.
lessons.application: When presenting a data-generation or pretraining method, define resource ranges and report how performance or behavior changes across them, with a relevant baseline condition.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the work has no meaningful scaling variable or lacks measurements across the proposed range.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide classification performance values, baselines, statistical uncertainty, or details of the architectures and pretraining approaches tested.
It does not specify how causal coherence, realism, sample efficiency, or the reported scaling laws were measured.
